newsitem.title: INDIA: Malhotra, author of India insurance reforms, dead.
newsitem.headline: Malhotra, author of India insurance reforms, dead.

text.p: Former Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Ram Nath Malhotra died in New Delhi on Tuesday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said. He was 71.
The funeral would be held later on Tuesday at 1600 hours in New Delhi, PTI said.
Malhotra was RBI governor from 1985 to 1990, a later authored a government-sponsored study to privatise India's insurance sector.
He also served as executive director of the International Monetary Fund representing India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Bhutan from November 1982 to February 1985.

The Malhotra Committee report he submitted in 1993 triggered an as yet inconclusive debate on the fate of India's state-run insurance business, an issue expected to engage parliament when it votes on the budget for 1997/98 (April-March) next month.
Malhotra argued that the Indian public wanted the insurance sector to be opened up to private participation.
He said the state sector should be given greater autonomy as the industry is opened up to private competition.
"About 60 to 65 percent preferred a mixed scenario of both public and private sectors competing," he said of his report.
The Malhotra Committee has since been disbanded.
Former finance minister P.Chidambaram's budget proposals, presented in February, have sought the opening up of health insurance to the private sector.
The move has been opposed by leftist constituents of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front alliance.
India is one of the least insured markets of the world and ranks 57th among 60 countries with per capital gross premium working out to $5 compared to $30 in Thailand and $407 in Taiwan.
Only around 10 million people are covered under life insurance out of a total population of 930 million.
